key_insight: A mixed hard/soft constraint workflow (instead of only rigid rules or opaque numeric weights) helps end users express intent, verify plans, and iteratively relax requirements so LLM-based planners become both controllable and adaptable.
problem_solved: Makes constraint specification and verification for LLM planning usable: addresses that hard-only constraints are too brittle and numeric flexibility weights confuse users, preventing reliable control and real-world adaptation.
method: Design of U-Define — an interaction workflow and UI that lets users declare hard constraints (must-have) and human-readable soft constraints (preferences) and combine them in readable templates.
Provide workflow primitives: simulate/verify plans against constraints, present alternative plans with graded violations, and enable progressive relaxation or re-ranking of soft constraints.
Evaluate via prototyping and user studies to compare usability, interpretability, and ability to recover valid plans versus hard-only or weight-only approaches.
impact: Enables practitioners to build LLM planning systems that are more predictable, debuggable, and usable by non-expert users; improves practical deployment of constraint-aware LLM pipelines in real-world tasks.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: specify constraints → verify/simulate → relax/re-rank → finalize plan (loop)
Before vs after comparison: hard-only vs U-Define mixed constraints showing success/failure cases
UI mockup: constraint editor with toggleable hard/soft flags and example-driven soft preference fields
Bar/line chart: usability/accuracy improvements (e.g., fewer failures, lower confusion) for mixed-workflow vs baselines
paper_title: U-Define: Designing User Workflows for Hard and Soft Constraints in LLM-Based Planning
paper_authors: Christine P Lee, Xinyu Jessica Wang, Aws Albarghouthi, David Porfirio, Bilge Mutlu
